about: Permit2 EIP-712 test vectors. Inputs only; the expected digests in permit2-vectors.json are derived from this file by verify_ours.py --emit and cross-checked by verify_sdk.mjs.
note_spender: For AllowanceTransfer, `spender` is a field of the signed struct and lives inside `message`. For SignatureTransfer it is NOT a struct field: PermitHash.hash() substitutes msg.sender, so it lives at case level. That asymmetry is the contract's, not ours.

cases.why: Byte-for-byte the vector published in SPEC-permit2-eip712 on 2026-08-05. If this one ever moves, either the old spec or this file is wrong.
amount = type(uint160).max. AllowanceTransfer._transfer skips the decrement entirely at this value, so the allowance never depletes. The policy refuses this one.

expiration = 0 is the SAFEST value, not the most dangerous: Allowance.updateAll stores uint48(block.timestamp), so the approval dies in the block that set it. A policy that rejects 0 is broken, not strict.
expiration = type(uint48).max (year 8921921). Not infinite by the contract's own test, but infinite in practice — the case an absolute ceiling in policy has to catch.
Same shape on Base. Only chainId changed, and the digest is completely different — the domain separator carries it.
PermitDetails[] enters as keccak of the concatenated member hashes, not as the members inline.
SignatureTransfer.PermitTransferFrom. `spender` is not in the struct — the contract hashes msg.sender in its place.
nonce = 500 -> wordPos 1, bitPos 244 in the unordered bitmap. Exercises a nonce that is not in word 0, which is where a naive implementation stops.
TokenPermissions[] array encoding, and the case where the spender may transfer a strict subset (requestedAmount = 0 is allowed per element).

The only Permit2 shape in which the destination of the funds is inside the signature — because the integrator put it there, in the witness. Type string order is alphabetical: SwapIntent before TokenPermissions.
cases.witnessTypeString: SwapIntent witness)SwapIntent(address recipient,address tokenOut,uint256 minAmountOut)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)

cases.why: Batch witness uses a different stub string. Reusing the single stub here produces a valid signature that the contract rejects.
cases.witnessTypeString: SwapIntent witness)SwapIntent(address recipient,address tokenOut,uint256 minAmountOut)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)

note_integers: Every integer is a decimal STRING. JSON numbers are IEEE-754 doubles in JavaScript: JSON.parse turns type(uint160).max into ...976, one more than the real value, and that is exactly the value that separates an infinite Permit2 approval from a finite one. Python's json would have parsed it exactly, so the two paths silently disagreed until this was fixed.
